name: BMI160 6-axis IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope)
description: Bosch Sensortec 16-bit 3-axis accelerometer (±2/4/8/16 g) and 3-axis gyroscope (±125 to ±2000 °/s) with an I2C/SPI interface and an on-chip temperature sensor. Sold as: GY-BMI160 purple module (12 pins on two edges: VIN, 3V3, GND, SCL, SDA, CS, SAO and OCS, INT2, INT1, SCX, SDX; 3.3 V LDO and 10 kΩ pull-ups on SDA, SCL, CS and SAO), I2C address 0x69 (0x68 with SAO tied to GND).
eli5: Feels which way is down and how fast it is turning, so your board knows tilt, shakes and spins.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply into the on-board 3.3 V regulator, 3.3–5 V (vendor rating 3–5 V)

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Regulator output / direct 3.3 V supply to the chip (max 3.6 V). Leave unconnected when VIN is used

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (SPI SCK); 10 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (SPI MOSI); 10 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on the board

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Chip select (CSB). Pulled up on the board = I2C mode; leave unconnected for I2C

pins.name: SAO
pins.description: Address select (chip SDO, SPI MISO): pulled up on the board = 0x69, tie to GND for 0x68

pins.name: OCS
pins.description: OCSB, secondary (OIS) SPI chip select. Not used for basic use

pins.name: INT2
pins.description: Interrupt output 2 (programmable). Not needed for basic use

pins.name: INT1
pins.description: Interrupt output 1 (programmable). Not needed for basic use

pins.name: SCX
pins.description: ASCX, auxiliary magnetometer interface clock. Not used for basic use

pins.name: SDX
pins.description: ASDX, auxiliary magnetometer interface data. Not used for basic use

buildNotes: The GY-BMI160 pulls SAO up, so it answers at 0x69. Tie SAO to GND for 0x68 (e.g. a second sensor on the bus at the other address).
Both sensors start in suspend mode and read zero until you write 0x11 (accel normal, wait 3.8 ms) and 0x15 (gyro normal, wait 80 ms) to CMD register 0x7E.
Data is little-endian, two's complement: gyro X/Y/Z at 0x0C-0x11, accel X/Y/Z at 0x12-0x17. Default ranges ±2 g (16384 LSB/g) and ±2000 °/s (16.4 LSB/°/s).
Power it from VIN (3.3–5 V) or from 3V3 (3.3 V only, max 3.6 V), not both. Leave CS unconnected for I2C: the board pulls it high.
The temperature register (0x20) is the die temperature, 23 °C + raw/512, valid only while the gyro runs.

driver.code:
# BMI160 6-axis IMU (Bosch Sensortec BMI160), MicroPython I2C driver.
# Written from the datasheet BST-BMI160-DS000-09: chip id 0xD1 in register 0x00,
# CMD register 0x7E (softreset 0xB6, accel normal 0x11, gyro normal 0x15),
# data registers 0x0C-0x17 (gyro X,Y,Z then accel X,Y,Z, 16-bit two's complement, LSB first),
# temperature 0x20-0x21 (0x0000 = 23 degC, 1/512 K per LSB, valid while the gyro is in normal mode).
import time

_CHIP_ID = 0x00
_DATA_GYR = 0x0C
_TEMP = 0x20
_ACC_RANGE = 0x41
_GYR_RANGE = 0x43
_CMD = 0x7E

# ACC_RANGE code -> LSB per g; GYR_RANGE code -> LSB per deg/s (datasheet tables)
_ACC = {2: (0x03, 16384.0), 4: (0x05, 8192.0), 8: (0x08, 4096.0), 16: (0x0C, 2048.0)}
_GYR = {2000: (0x00, 16.4), 1000: (0x01, 32.8), 500: (0x02, 65.6), 250: (0x03, 131.2), 125: (0x04, 262.4)}


def _s16(lo, hi):
    v = lo | (hi << 8)
    return v - 65536 if v & 0x8000 else v


class BMI160:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x69, accel_range=2, gyro_range=2000):
        # GY-BMI160: SAO is pulled up on the board, so the address is 0x69 unless SAO is tied to GND (0x68).
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        cid = self._r(_CHIP_ID, 1)[0]
        if cid != 0xD1:
            raise OSError('BMI160 not found (chip id 0x%02X): check wiring and address' % cid)
        self._w(_CMD, 0xB6)      # softreset
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        self._w(_CMD, 0x11)      # accelerometer -> normal mode (max 3.8 ms)
        time.sleep_ms(5)
        self._w(_CMD, 0x15)      # gyroscope -> normal mode (max 80 ms)
        time.sleep_ms(100)
        code, self._acc_lsb = _ACC[accel_range]
        self._w(_ACC_RANGE, code)
        code, self._gyr_lsb = _GYR[gyro_range]
        self._w(_GYR_RANGE, code)
        time.sleep_ms(10)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def _r(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def read(self):
        """Return ((ax, ay, az) in g, (gx, gy, gz) in deg/s), read in one burst."""
        d = self._r(_DATA_GYR, 12)
        g = tuple(_s16(d[i], d[i + 1]) / self._gyr_lsb for i in (0, 2, 4))
        a = tuple(_s16(d[i], d[i + 1]) / self._acc_lsb for i in (6, 8, 10))
        return a, g

    def acceleration(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def gyro(self):
        return self.read()[1]

    def temperature(self):
        """Die temperature in degC."""
        d = self._r(_TEMP, 2)
        return 23 + _s16(d[0], d[1]) / 512

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from bmi160 import BMI160

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
imu = BMI160(i2c)  # 0x69 on the GY-BMI160 (SAO pulled up)
while True:
    (ax, ay, az), (gx, gy, gz) = imu.read()
    print('A=%.2f,%.2f,%.2fg G=%.1f,%.1f,%.1fdps T=%.1fC' % (ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, imu.temperature()))
    time.sleep(1)
